newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - FASHION LOSSES RIP INTO KBB'S 1996/97 NET.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - FASHION LOSSES RIP INTO KBB'S 1996/97 NET.

text.p: Dutch stores group Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer(KBB) said on Friday ordinary net profit slumped 37 percent to 61.7 million guilders in 1996/97, as loss-making fashion unit M&S Mode tore into its bottom line.

"KBB's other three main chains -- Hema, Bijenkorf and Praxis -- performed well in the area of sales, profit and strategy, but M&S was the fly in the ointment," KBB chairman Theo Henselijn told a results news conference.
The group warned in January that its 1996 results would be hit by problems at fashion store chain M&S Mode, saying it expected total net profits around 61 million guilders.
KBB cut its dividend to 3.00 guilders per share over the 1996/97 year ended January 31 from a previous 3.40 pay-out.

Turnover at its upmarket Bijenkorf department store chain rose 4.4 percent to 829.5 million guilders, at mid-range general retailer Hema by 5.3 percent to 2.38 billion and at DIY chain Praxis by 12 percent to 1.20 billion.

But although turnover at M&S Mode increased to 706.1 million guilders from 622.2 million the previous year, the fashion chain suffered a loss equivalent to its average annual operating profit in previous years.

Asked to specify the loss, board member Peter Dirks conceded it was "in the region" of some 50 million guilders. Total operating profit at KBB's specialty stores plunged to 20.9 million guilders from a year-earlier 103.8 million.
Henselijn said bad internal communication had led to mistakes being made in adapting the M&S formula.
"M&S was a terrible disappointment. The strategy was good, but it was carried out in an unbalanced way," Henselijn said.
He said the chain targeted slightly overweight women in their forties or older, and had been forced to adjust its purchasing strategies to the more youthful style of dressing adopted by this group.
But purchasers had adapted the collection too rapidly and in a way insufficiently well-tuned to the target group, he said.
Henselijn said M&S Mode had planned 25 percent sales growth, but had been forced to sell some 12 percent of its inventory at bargain basement prices, resulting in sharply narrower margins.
"The purchase system is fine as long as things go well, but if there's a problem, there's little one can do," Dirks added.
M&S collections were previously bought 12 months in advance in order to secure a discount.

In addition, fully analysed data regarding the returns in a particular month only became available in the third week of the following month, Dirks said. This had been a factor in the relatively late profit warning of last October, he said.
KBB now aims to reduce M&S purchasing times and review the chain's collection once again. It has appointed a new head at the M&S chain.

"The large number of shops in Germany, where the situation remains poor, is an additional handicap," Henselijn said. He said M&S would halt further expansion until it returned to profit, but added prior commitments obliged them to open an additional 20 stores, of which an undisclosed number in Germany.
Results are set to recover in 1997/98, but KBB declined to give an estimate of the size of recovery.

"Because the pace of profit recovery at M&S is uncertain and the two last months of the year are of decisive importance for the annual result, no forecast can yet be given over the size of the profit recovery of the group," Henselijn said.
With no extraordinary items, KBB's total net profit was down 58 percent from 146.2 million guilders in 1995, when the group realised an extraordinary gain of 47.6 million from disposals.
KBB shares were down 1.00 guilders at 133.00 in a slow Amsterdam market at 1135 GMT on Friday.
